messages:
karen-kotlin: quick note — I hit a flaky where cancelling a suspend Retrofit call doesn't always abort the underlying OkHttp call on emulator API 30. under load this leads to dispatcher saturation.

karen-kotlin: reproduce: wrap suspend adapter call with withTimeout(800) and hammer with 20 concurrent callers. ~5% of runs show coroutine cancelled but OkHttp still logs response 2-3s later.

karen-kotlin: minimal repro snippet:
```
withTimeout(800) { api.predict(input) }
// adapter enqueues call and cancels on continuation cancellation
```

tom-qa: logs?

karen-kotlin:
```
I/Coroutine: cancelled by timeout
I/OkHttp: --> POST /v1/predict
I/OkHttp: <-- 200 (2500ms)
```

jess-platform: likely race between continuation cancel -> call.cancel() and native socket write in streaming body. OkHttp may not interrupt immediately on some Android kernels. Two pragmatic fixes: (1) propagate coroutine deadline into OkHttp call.timeout() before enqueue; (2) add a short watchdog in SDK that observes dispatcher.runningCalls growth and surfaces early error.

tom-qa: (2) seems brittle. prefer (1) + test coverage across emulator matrix.

karen-kotlin: implemented (1) in adapter: if caller coroutine has a Timeout or deadline, set call.timeout().timeout(remainingMs, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) before enqueue and still call.cancel() on cancellation. Quick local results look promising.

jess-platform: nice. also add docs snippet and mirror change in Java SDK for parity. Add unit harness that simulates streaming body and asserts call finishes within 200ms of coroutine cancel.

ci-bot: queued emulator-matrix job: cancel-propagation (id 9402).

tom-qa: I'll add the flaky test to the emulator pipeline (API 28-34). Will flag if we still see failures.

karen-kotlin: PR incoming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-kotlin/pull/1482 — includes adapter fix, test harness, and docs.

jess-platform: thanks — will review and ensure Java parity. Also add a note in SDK docs: "Cancellation is best-effort; use per-call timeout propagation for more deterministic behavior across Android releases."

karen-kotlin: done, thanks.
